objective.description: For each query, compute the number of distinct final service point sequences (under the allowed reordering) that achieve the maximum possible total duration of the first k points. Output the count modulo 1,000,000,007.

rule_selection_reason: existence_to_counting can transform the maximization problem into a counting problem with well-defined equivalence classes, while minimum_guarantee_under_perturbation is not applicable because the seed problem lacks an inherent perturbation model—any disturbance would be artificial.；创新度判断：Shifts the core obligation from finding the maximum sum to counting all distinct rearrangements achieving that maximum, introducing new responsibilities like defining counting objects, handling duplicates, and setting deduplication rules.；难度判断：Requires combinatorial counting, including managing permutations of identical values, precomputing factorials and modular inverses, and efficiently answering per-query counts without exceeding time limits.；风险判断：The risk is that counting reduces to a simple combinatorial formula without changing the solution structure, but explicit deduplication requirements and invariant changes can prevent this.

components.role_description: Queries, each with service type code p and number of points k

constraints.name: reorderable_set_condition
constraints.description: Only service points whose duration is divisible by the type code p can be reordered; the relative positions of all other points remain fixed.
constraints.formal: For a given query (p, k), let S = {i | p divides M_i}. Any valid rearrangement M' must satisfy M'_i = M_i for i ∉ S, and {M'_i : i ∈ S} = {M_i : i ∈ S} as a multiset.

constraints.name: prefix_selection
constraints.description: The resident experiences the first k points in order; the total service duration is the sum of the first k elements of the rearranged list.

constraints.name: prime_ingredient
constraints.description: The service type code p in each query is a prime number.

constraints.name: independent_queries
constraints.description: Each query is independent; any rearrangement performed for one query does not affect the original list for other queries.
constraints.formal: For each query, the rearrangement starts from the original list M.

constraints.name: counting_unit
constraints.description: Two rearranged lists M' and M'' are considered the same if they are identical as arrays. The answer counts distinct final arrays.
constraints.formal: M'_i = M''_i for all i implies they are the same. Only distinct arrays contribute to the count.

constraints.name: finite_solution_space
constraints.description: Because there are only finitely many points and permutations of the movable ones are finite, the number of distinct valid rearrangements is finite, and the answer is computed modulo a large prime.

constraints.name: threshold_property
constraints.description: For an optimal rearrangement (maximizing sum of first k), there exists a threshold value t such that all movable elements with value > t must appear in the first k movable slots, all with value < t must appear after, and exactly r of those with value = t are in the first k, where r = (number of movable slots in first k) - count of movable elements with value > t.
constraints.formal: Let c_k = |S ∩ {1..k}|, let sorted values of S be d_1 ≥ ... ≥ d_m. Set t = d_{c_k}, and let r = c_k - #{i: d_i > t}. Then in any optimal M', the multiset of values in S∩{1..k} consists of all d_i > t and exactly r copies of t.

objective.description: For each query, compute the number of distinct final service point sequences (under the allowed reordering) that achieve the maximum possible total duration of the first k points. Output the count modulo 1,000,000,007.

invariants.name: prefix_movable_count_invariance
invariants.description: The number of movable elements in any prefix of length k is invariant under valid reorderings, because only movable elements can change position but their set remains the same. This quantity determines how many movable slots must be filled with the largest elements to maximize the prefix sum.

invariants.name: optimal_front_multiset
invariants.description: In any rearrangement achieving the maximum prefix sum, the multiset of values assigned to the first k movable slots is uniquely determined (up to permutation of identical values). It consists of all movable elements strictly greater than the threshold value t, plus a specific number r of elements equal to t, where t is the c_k-th largest movable element. This invariant ensures that all optimal rearrangements share the same front multiset, enabling combinatorial counting of distinct sequences.

algorithmic_delta_claim.seed_solver_core: For each prime p appearing in values, collect all indices and values of elements divisible by p. Sort these values in descending order and compute prefix sums. Also maintain an array of fixed prefix sums of the original menu. For a query (p,k), count how many of the first k elements are movable (using binary search on index list). Let this count be c. The maximum sum = fixed_prefix_sum[k] - sum of original movable values in first k + sum of largest c movable values globally.
algorithmic_delta_claim.reusable_subroutines: Preprocessing: prime factorisation per element, building lists per p of (value, index), sorting values descending, building index arrays, computing prefix sums of these sorted values and of the original menu. Binary search to find number of movable elements in first k. All these are directly reused.
algorithmic_delta_claim.new_solver_core: Extend preprocessing: for each prime p, build a frequency map of values and precompute the product of inverse factorials of these counts, P_p. Precompute factorials and inverse factorials up to N. For each query, after finding c and the sorted movable list, identify the threshold value t (the c-th largest) and r = c - count of values > t. Then compute answer = factorial(c) * factorial(m - c) * P_p * factorial(count[t]) * inv_factorial(r) * inv_factorial(count[t] - r) mod MOD. This counts distinct optimal sequences.
algorithmic_delta_claim.new_proof_obligation: Show that the front multiset is uniquely determined in any optimal sequence, and that the formula correctly counts distinct final arrays (i.e., identical arrays induced by different permutations of same-valued elements are not double-counted). Also prove that no additional optimal sequences exist beyond those described.
algorithmic_delta_claim.why_direct_reuse_fails: The original solver produces a single numeric value (the maximum sum). It has no mechanism for counting multiple achieving sequences or handling deduplication. Direct reuse would only give the maximum, not the count, and cannot account for the combinatorial structure of the solution space.

generated_problem.title: 社区服务的排班方案
generated_problem.description:
幸福社区有 N 个服务点，编号 1 到 N。每个服务点 i 有一个固定的服务时长 M_i。住户会按顺序依次访问前 k 个服务点。社区管理员可以为每位住户调整部分服务点的顺序，但只能调整那些服务时长能被质数 p 整除的服务点（称为灵活服务点），其余服务点的相对顺序保持不变。每次调整从原始顺序开始，各个查询相互独立。
对于每个查询 (p, k)，你需要计算：在所有能使前 k 个服务点的服务时长之和达到最大的重排方案中，有多少种不同的最终服务点序列？如果两个序列在某个位置上的服务时长不同，则认为它们不同。答案可能很大，请将其对 1,000,000,007 取模后输出。
generated_problem.input_format:
第一行一个整数 T，表示测试用例数量。
接下来每个测试用例：
  第一行一个整数 N，表示服务点的数量。
  第二行 N 个由空格分隔的整数 M_1, M_2, ..., M_N，分别表示每个服务点的服务时长。
  第三行一个整数 Q，表示查询的数量。
  接下来 Q 行，每行两个整数 p 和 k，表示一个查询：p 是一个质数，表示住户关注的类型；k 是该住户将访问的前 k 个服务点。
generated_problem.output_format: 对于每个测试用例，依次输出每个查询的答案，每个答案占一行，表示达到最大总服务时长的不同最终序列的数目，结果对 1,000,000,007 取模。
constraints: 所有测试用例的 N 总和不超过 2×10^5
所有测试用例的 Q 总和不超过 2×10^5

samples.explanation:
原始序列 [2,4,4,6]。
对于第一个查询 p=2, k=3：所有服务点均可被 2 整除，灵活服务点为索引 1,2,3,4。前 3 个位置中有 3 个灵活位置。为使前 3 项之和最大，必须将最大的 3 个灵活时长 6,4,4 放到前三个位置。它们的不同排列数为 3! / 2! = 3，对应的最终序列为 [6,4,4,2]、[4,6,4,2]、[4,4,6,2]。
对于第二个查询 p=2, k=2：灵活服务点同上，前 2 个位置中有 2 个灵活位置。最优前缀必须包含 6 和一个 4。前两个位置可以是 (6,4) 或 (4,6)，后两个位置剩余一个 4 和 2，可以任意排列。但由于存在两个相同的 4，最终不同的完整序列有 4 种：[6,4,4,2]、[6,4,2,4]、[4,6,4,2]、[4,6,2,4]。
原始序列 [3,3,3,6,9]，质数 p=3，k=5。所有服务时长都能被 3 整除，因此所有服务点都是灵活服务点。为使前 5 项之和最大，可以将所有点按任意顺序重排，不同序列数即为 5 个元素的全排列去除重复值：5! / 3! = 20。因此答案为 20。

generated_problem.notes: 每个查询中的 p 均为质数。答案需要对 1,000,000,007 取模。达到最大总时长的方案总是存在，并且可以通过题目描述的贪心构造得到。计数时需考虑重复值导致的去重，即仅当数组完全一致时才视为同一个序列。
